'''David Catrow''' (born December 16, 1952) <!-- source is Ext link LCCN --> is an American artist,<!--2014-08-20, "artist" may be misleading; are these all children's picture books? is there no collection of editorial cartoons? --> [[cartoonist]], and illustrator of [[Children's literature|children's books]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Cole|first=Dianne|title=For Kids, Just Plain Fun Is a Comfort and a Joy|url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=6499000|accessdate=October 4, 2013|publisher=NPR|date=November 28, 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Rose|first=Alan|title=Illustrator Catrow helps children see big picture|url=http://texas.rangers.mlb.com/news/article.jsp?ymd=20111208&content_id=26133142&vkey=news_tex&c_id=tex|publisher=Texas Rangers|accessdate=October 4, 2013}}{{dead link|date=October 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Page Turners|url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=VP&p_theme=vp&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=103D352254D588D7&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM|accessdate=October 4, 2013|newspaper=Virginian-Pilot|date=July 13, 2004}}</ref>

Catrow has illustrated over 60 children's books and prior to this, worked as a cartoonist at the ''[[Springfield News-Sun]]'' (Ohio).<ref>{{cite news|title=WASSO salutes cartoonist and illustrator David Catrow|url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=SNSB&p_theme=snsb&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=1270FA6579991630&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM|accessdate=October 4, 2013|newspaper=News-Sun|date=March 22, 2009}}</ref> His illustrations for the book ''She's Wearing a Dead Bird on Her Head!'' was one of [[The New York Times]] "Best Illustrated Books of the Year" for 1995.<ref>{{cite news|title=The Best Illustrated Books of the Year|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/11/12/books/the-best-illustrated-books-of-the-year.html|accessdate=October 4, 2013|newspaper=The New York Times|date=November 12, 1995}}</ref> He was the illustrator for ''[[How Murray Saved Christmas]]'' written by [[Mike Reiss]] which was adapted into a 2014 animated television special of the same name which aired on [[NBC]].

Catrow has also served as a visual developer for animated films, including films such as ''[[Despicable Me]]'' and ''[[Horton Hears a Who! (film)|Horton Hears a Who!]]''.<ref name="About Me">[https://www.catrow.com/about-me David Catrow - About Me]</ref>{{third party inline|date=November 2022}}

He and his wife, Deborah, live in Springfield, Ohio and have two children.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.scholastic.com/content/teachers/en/authors/david-catrow/|title=David Catrow Books, Author Biography, and Reading Level {{!}} Scholastic|website=www.scholastic.com|access-date=2019-08-15}}</ref>
